de.title: B1 Đọc phần 1 · 5 tin ngắn
de.gist: Five short real-world texts: a sign, a text message, a note, an email and a notice.
de.vi: Đọc từng tin ngắn, chọn câu nói đúng ý tin.

groups.inst: For each question, choose the correct answer.

items.q:
SWIMMING POOL
Children under 8 must be with an adult in the water at all times.
What does the notice say?
o: Young children need an adult beside them while swimming.
Children under 8 cannot use the pool.
Adults should not swim with children.
items.a: Young children need an adult beside them while swimming.
items.why_vi: "must be with an adult in the water at all times" = luôn phải có người lớn cùng xuống nước. Không cấm trẻ em, cũng không cấm người lớn bơi cùng.

items.q:
Mia, the 6:15 bus is cancelled, so I'll be at the café about 40 minutes late. Order without me if you're hungry! Sam
Why did Sam write this message?
o: To change the place where they will meet
To tell Mia he will arrive later than planned
To ask Mia to buy food for him
items.a: To tell Mia he will arrive later than planned
items.why_vi: Xe buýt bị huỷ nên Sam tới trễ khoảng 40 phút. Chỗ hẹn vẫn là quán cà phê; Sam bảo Mia cứ gọi món, không nhờ mua đồ ăn.

items.q:
Gym members: from Monday, please book classes online. Phone bookings will no longer be accepted.
What is changing at the gym?
o: Members can only book classes on the website.
The gym is closing its phone line for repairs.
items.a: Members can only book classes on the website.
items.why_vi: Từ thứ Hai đặt lớp trực tuyến, không nhận đặt qua điện thoại nữa. Lớp không phải mới bắt đầu.

items.q:
Dad, I've borrowed your bike because mine has a flat tyre. I'll fix mine this weekend. Leo
What does Leo say?
o: He has repaired his father's bike.
He will use his father's bike until his own is fixed.
He wants to buy a new tyre for his father.
items.a: He will use his father's bike until his own is fixed.
items.why_vi: Xe của Leo bị xẹp lốp nên mượn xe bố, cuối tuần sẽ sửa xe mình. Leo không sửa xe bố.

items.q:
LIBRARY
Books returned after the due date: 20p per day. Children's books: no charge.
What does the notice tell you?
o: You pay for late adult books but not late children's books.
All books must be returned within 20 days.
items.a: You pay for late adult books but not late children's books.
items.why_vi: Trả sách trễ mất 20 xu mỗi ngày, riêng sách thiếu nhi không mất tiền. "20p" là tiền, không phải 20 ngày.

de.title: B1 Đọc phần 5 · The town that grows its own food
de.topic: A town that grows vegetables in public places
de.gist: A short article about a town where vegetables are grown in public spaces for anyone to pick.
de.vi: Đọc bài, chọn từ đúng cho 6 chỗ trống.
de.text:
The town that grows its own food

Ten years ago, a small group of people in the English town of Todmorden had an unusual idea. They [1] planting vegetables in public places, such as outside the police station and next to the bus stop. Anyone was allowed to pick the food for free.

At first, many people did not [2] what was happening. Some thought the plants were only for decoration. But slowly, the idea became popular. Local schools [3] part, and children learned how to grow beans and tomatoes.

Today, visitors come from all over the world to see the gardens. The project has also [4] the town in other ways. Local shops now sell more food that is grown nearby, and people say they [5] their neighbours better than before. The organisers believe that growing food together is a simple way to [6] a community stronger.

groups.inst: Read the text and choose the correct word for each space.

items.q: Gap 1
items.why_vi: "began planting" = bắt đầu trồng (begin + V-ing). "set" cần "set about"; "opened", "made" không đi với V-ing này.

items.q: Gap 2
items.why_vi: Câu sau nói có người tưởng cây chỉ để trang trí, tức họ chưa "understand" (hiểu) chuyện gì đang xảy ra. Các từ khác không hợp nghĩa.

items.q: Gap 3
items.why_vi: Cụm cố định "take part" = tham gia. "joined" không đi với "part".

items.q: Gap 4
items.why_vi: "has also helped the town in other ways" = còn giúp thị trấn theo những cách khác. "made / let / given" không đi được với cấu trúc này.

items.q: Gap 5
items.why_vi: "know their neighbours better" = hiểu hàng xóm hơn. "meet … better" không dùng.

items.q: Gap 6
items.why_vi: Cấu trúc "make + tân ngữ + tính từ": "make a community stronger".

de.title: B1 Đọc phần 6 · Email từ trại hè
de.topic: An email from a summer camp
de.gist: An email to a friend about a week at a summer camp.
de.vi: Đọc email, điền MỘT từ vào mỗi chỗ trống.
de.text:
Hi Jess,

I'm writing to you from the summer camp! I arrived [1] Saturday, and I've already made lots of new friends. There are about sixty of us here, and we all sleep in wooden cabins near the lake.

Every morning we go kayaking, and in the afternoon we can choose between climbing, art or football. Yesterday I tried climbing for the first time. It was much harder [2] I expected, but I got to the top in the end!

The food is better than I thought it would be, although there isn't [3] choice for vegetarians. My favourite part of the day is the evening, [4] we sit around the fire and sing songs.

I really think you would enjoy it here. [5] you want, I can send you the website so you can come with me next year. Write back soon and tell me what you have [6] doing!

Love,
Anna

groups.inst: For each space, write ONE word.

items.q: Gap 1
items.why_vi: Trước thứ trong tuần dùng giới từ "on": "on Saturday". "last Saturday" (thứ Bảy vừa rồi) cũng đúng.

items.q: Gap 2
items.why_vi: Sau so sánh hơn "harder" là "than": "harder than I expected".

items.q: Gap 3
items.why_vi: "choice" ở đây không đếm được, câu phủ định dùng "much": "there isn't much choice". "a choice" cũng chấp nhận được.

items.q: Gap 4
items.why_vi: Mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ thời gian bổ nghĩa cho "the evening": "when we sit around the fire".

items.q: Gap 5
items.why_vi: Câu điều kiện: "If you want, I can send you the website" (nếu bạn muốn).

items.q: Gap 6
items.why_vi: Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn "what you have been doing" (dạo này bạn làm gì).

de.part: B2 First · Reading and Use of English Part 1
de.title: B2 Use of English phần 1 · The quiet carriage
de.gist: An article about quiet carriages on trains and why passengers value them.
de.vi: Đọc bài, chọn từ đúng cho 8 chỗ trống.
de.text:
The quiet carriage

Many train companies now offer a quiet carriage, where passengers are asked not to make phone calls or play music out loud. The idea was first [1] as a small experiment, but it has become extremely popular with people who want to work or simply rest during their journey.

Of course, not everyone [2] by the rules. Some passengers say they did not notice the signs, while others seem to think a short call does not [3] as breaking them. Train staff are usually reluctant to get involved, so it is often left to other travellers to [4] the problem.

Researchers who studied passenger behaviour found that people who sit in the quiet carriage are more likely to [5] on a task than those in ordinary carriages. They also reported feeling less tired at the end of the journey. [6] the occasional argument, most regular users believe the quiet carriage is worth defending.

Some companies are now considering [7] the idea further, with "quiet zones" in stations. Whether these will catch [8] remains to be seen.

groups.inst: Read the text and decide which answer best fits each gap.

items.q: Gap 1
items.why_vi: "an idea was introduced as an experiment" = được đưa ra thử nghiệm. "founded" dùng cho tổ chức, "appeared" không có bị động.

items.q: Gap 2
items.why_vi: Chỉ "abide" đi với giới từ "by": "abide by the rules" (tuân theo luật). "follows / obeys / keeps" không cần "by".

items.q: Gap 3
items.why_vi: "count as" = được tính là: "a short call does not count as breaking them" (cuộc gọi ngắn không bị coi là phạm luật). "regard / consider / see" cần tân ngữ: "regard something as".

items.q: Gap 4
items.why_vi: "deal with the problem" = xử lý vấn đề. "put up with" là chịu đựng, trái ý; "come up with" là nghĩ ra.

items.q: Gap 5
items.why_vi: "concentrate on a task" = tập trung vào việc. "devote" cần "to" và tân ngữ, "attend" cần "to", "pay" cần "attention".

items.q: Gap 6
items.why_vi: Trước cụm danh từ "the occasional argument" dùng "Despite". "Although" cần mệnh đề, "However" không đứng như vậy.

items.q: Gap 7
items.why_vi: Cụm "take an idea further" = phát triển ý tưởng thêm. "consider" đi với V-ing.

items.q: Gap 8
items.why_vi: Cụm động từ "catch on" = trở nên phổ biến.

de.part: B2 First · Reading and Use of English Part 3
de.title: B2 Use of English phần 3 · Learning to juggle
de.topic: Learning to juggle as an adult
de.gist: An article about adults who take up juggling and what it does for the brain.
de.vi: Đọc bài, dùng từ IN HOA cuối dòng để tạo từ đúng cho 8 chỗ trống.
de.text:
Learning to juggle

Juggling may look like a skill that only circus [1] need, but more and more adults are taking it up as a hobby. (PERFORM)
Beginners usually start with three soft balls, and the first few weeks can be [2] frustrating. (SURPRISE)
Most people drop the balls again and again, and some give up out of [3]. (BORED)
However, those who keep going often describe a real sense of [4] when they finally manage a full minute. (ACHIEVE)
There is also some [5] that learning a new physical skill can be good for the brain. (EVIDENT)
In one study, adults who practised for six weeks showed changes in areas linked to vision and [6]. (MOVE)
Teachers say that patience is more important than natural [7]. (ABLE)
And since the equipment is cheap and the hobby can be done almost anywhere, it is hardly [8] that clubs are appearing in many cities. (SURPRISE)

groups.inst: Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits in the gap.

items.q: Gap 1 (PERFORM)
items.why_vi: Cần danh từ số nhiều chỉ người: "circus performers" (diễn viên xiếc).

items.q: Gap 2 (SURPRISE)
items.why_vi: Bổ nghĩa cho tính từ "frustrating" cần trạng từ: "surprisingly frustrating".

items.q: Gap 3 (BORED)
items.why_vi: Sau "out of" cần danh từ: "out of boredom" (vì chán).

items.q: Gap 4 (ACHIEVE)
items.why_vi: "a sense of" + danh từ: "a sense of achievement" (cảm giác thành công).

items.q: Gap 5 (EVIDENT)
items.why_vi: "some" + danh từ không đếm được: "some evidence" (một số bằng chứng).

items.q: Gap 6 (MOVE)
items.why_vi: Song song với danh từ "vision": "vision and movement" (thị giác và vận động).

items.q: Gap 7 (ABLE)
items.why_vi: Sau tính từ "natural" cần danh từ: "natural ability" (năng khiếu).

items.q: Gap 8 (SURPRISE)
items.why_vi: "it is hardly + tính từ + that": "it is hardly surprising that" (chẳng có gì ngạc nhiên khi).

de.part: B2 First · Reading and Use of English Part 4
de.title: B2 Use of English phần 4 · Viết lại câu (bộ 1)
de.topic: Key word transformations about everyday situations
de.gist: Six key word transformation items about travel, work and study.
de.vi: Viết lại câu thứ hai cùng nghĩa câu đầu, dùng từ IN HOA, 2–5 từ.

groups.inst: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.

items.q:
I haven't been to the cinema for six months.
LAST
The ______ to the cinema was six months ago.
items.why_vi: "haven't … for six months" = "The last time I went … was six months ago".

items.q:
"Don't forget to lock the door," Maria told her brother.
REMINDED
Maria ______ the door.
items.why_vi: Câu tường thuật: "remind somebody to do something" = "reminded her brother to lock the door".

items.q:
It wasn't necessary for us to book a table.
NEED
We ______ a table.
items.why_vi: "It wasn't necessary" = "didn't need to book". "needn't have booked" cũng đúng (nhưng hàm ý đã đặt rồi).

items.q:
The concert was so popular that all the tickets sold out in an hour.
SUCH
It was ______ that all the tickets sold out in an hour.
items.why_vi: "so + tính từ" đổi thành "such + a + tính từ + danh từ": "such a popular concert".

items.q:
Tom started learning Spanish three years ago.
BEEN
Tom ______ Spanish for three years.
items.why_vi: Việc bắt đầu trong quá khứ và còn tiếp: hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn "has been learning … for three years".

items.q:
I regret not taking the job in London.
WISH
I ______ the job in London.
items.why_vi: Tiếc về quá khứ: "wish + quá khứ hoàn thành": "I wish I had taken the job".

de.title: How birds find their way
de.topic: How migrating birds find their way
de.gist: A passage on the senses migrating birds use to navigate: the sun, the stars, the magnetic field, smell and experience.
de.vi: Đọc bài, làm 13 câu: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN, điền câu, trắc nghiệm.
de.text:
How birds find their way

Every autumn, billions of birds leave their breeding grounds in the northern hemisphere and fly south, some travelling more than ten thousand kilometres. Many return the following spring not just to the same region but to the same garden, hedge or even nest. For centuries, people have wondered how such small animals manage these journeys, often across oceans and deserts, and frequently at night. Scientists now believe that birds do not rely on a single method. Instead, they appear to combine several different senses, switching from one to another depending on the conditions.

The sun is one of the most important guides for birds that migrate by day. However, the sun is not a fixed point: it moves across the sky from east to west. To use it as a compass, a bird must also know the time of day. Experiments with starlings in the 1950s showed that caged birds turned in the correct direction when they could see the sun. When their internal clock was shifted, by keeping them under artificial light at unusual hours, they chose the wrong direction by a predictable amount. This suggested that the birds were adjusting for the movement of the sun with a kind of biological clock.

Many songbirds, however, migrate at night. In the 1960s, researchers placed young birds of a night-migrating species inside a planetarium, where the pattern of stars on the ceiling could be controlled. When the artificial sky was made to turn around a different star, the birds learned to treat that point as north, even though it was not the real Pole Star. The study showed that birds are not born knowing the constellations. Instead, young birds learn which part of the night sky stays still while the rest of the stars rotate around it.

On cloudy nights, when neither the sun nor the stars are visible, many birds can still find their way. This is because they are able to sense the magnetic field of the Earth. The exact mechanism is still debated. One theory is that light-sensitive molecules in the eyes of the bird react to the magnetic field, so that the bird may literally see magnetic directions as a pattern laid over its normal vision. Another theory focused on tiny particles of iron in the upper beak, although later studies found that many of these particles belonged to immune cells and were probably not involved in navigation at all.

A compass, though, only tells a bird which direction it is facing. To return to a particular place, it also needs something like a map. Homing pigeons, which can find their way back to their loft from hundreds of kilometres away, seem to use smell for this purpose. In experiments carried out in Italy, pigeons whose sense of smell had been temporarily blocked were much less successful at returning home than other pigeons released at the same site. It appears that pigeons learn how the mixture of smells in the air changes with the direction of the wind around their home area.

Experience also plays a part. In a famous experiment, thousands of starlings were caught in the Netherlands during their autumn migration and transported by plane to Switzerland before being released. Adult birds, which had made the journey before, corrected their course and headed towards their usual winter areas in France and southern England. Young birds on their first migration, however, simply continued flying in the same direction as before, and many ended up in Spain. This suggests that young birds follow an inherited direction and distance, while older birds have built up something like a mental map.

Modern technology is now allowing researchers to follow individual birds across entire journeys. Tracking devices weighing less than a gram can record the position of a bird, and some have revealed that birds make far fewer stops than expected. As the climate changes and artificial light spreads, understanding these navigation systems may become important for protecting migratory species, since bright city lights can confuse birds that travel at night. Some cities have already begun dimming the lights of tall buildings during the main migration seasons, and early results suggest that far fewer birds now crash into windows.

groups.inst: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

items.q: Some birds return to exactly the same place where they bred the previous year.
items.why_vi: Bài nói nhiều con quay về không chỉ cùng vùng mà cùng khu vườn, hàng rào, thậm chí cùng tổ.
items.ev: Many return the following spring not just to the same region but to the same garden, hedge or even nest.

items.q: Scientists think birds that migrate by day use only the sun to navigate.
items.why_vi: Bài nói chim không dựa vào một cách duy nhất mà kết hợp nhiều giác quan; mặt trời chỉ là "one of the most important guides". Chữ "only" trái với bài.
items.ev: Scientists now believe that birds do not rely on a single method.

items.q: Starlings whose internal clock had been shifted chose the wrong direction.
items.why_vi: Khi đồng hồ sinh học bị lệch, chim chọn sai hướng một lượng đoán trước được.
items.ev: When their internal clock was shifted, by keeping them under artificial light at unusual hours, they chose the wrong direction by a predictable amount.

items.q: The birds used in the planetarium study had already migrated before.
items.why_vi: Bài nói rõ là "young birds" (chim non), và nghiên cứu cho thấy chim học bầu trời đêm chứ không sinh ra đã biết.
items.ev: In the 1960s, researchers placed young birds of a night-migrating species inside a planetarium, where the pattern of stars on the ceiling could be controlled.

items.q: Birds navigate more accurately on cloudy nights than on clear nights.
items.why_vi: Bài chỉ nói chim vẫn tìm đường được khi trời nhiều mây (nhờ từ trường), không so sánh độ chính xác giữa đêm mây và đêm quang.

items.q: The pigeon experiments in Italy lasted for more than ten years.
items.why_vi: Bài có nhắc thí nghiệm ở Ý nhưng không nói kéo dài bao lâu.

groups.inst: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

items.q: One theory suggests that birds may see magnetic directions as a ______ over their normal vision.
items.why_vi: "see magnetic directions as a pattern laid over its normal vision".
items.ev: One theory is that light-sensitive molecules in the eyes of the bird react to the magnetic field, so that the bird may literally see magnetic directions as a pattern laid over its normal vision.

items.q: Many of the iron particles found in the beak turned out to belong to ______.
items.why_vi: "many of these particles belonged to immune cells" (tế bào miễn dịch), nên có lẽ không liên quan tới định hướng.
items.ev: Another theory focused on tiny particles of iron in the upper beak, although later studies found that many of these particles belonged to immune cells and were probably not involved in navigation at all.

items.q: Homing pigeons seem to rely on ______ to work out where they are.
items.why_vi: "seem to use smell for this purpose" (dùng khứu giác làm "bản đồ").
items.ev: Homing pigeons, which can find their way back to their loft from hundreds of kilometres away, seem to use smell for this purpose.

items.q: After being released in Switzerland, many young starlings ended up in ______.
items.why_vi: Chim non giữ nguyên hướng bay cũ nên nhiều con tới Tây Ban Nha; chim trưởng thành sửa hướng về Pháp và miền nam nước Anh.
items.ev: Young birds on their first migration, however, simply continued flying in the same direction as before, and many ended up in Spain.

groups.inst: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

items.q: Why must a bird know the time of day to use the sun as a compass?
o: because the sun changes its position during the day
because birds only fly in the early morning
because the sun is hidden at midday
because birds need to rest at regular times
items.a: because the sun changes its position during the day
items.why_vi: Mặt trời không đứng yên mà đi từ đông sang tây, nên chim phải biết giờ để bù cho chuyển động đó.
items.ev: However, the sun is not a fixed point: it moves across the sky from east to west.

items.q: What did the planetarium study show about young birds?
o: They are born knowing the constellations.
They learn which point in the night sky does not move.
They cannot find north without the real Pole Star.
They prefer artificial skies to real ones.
items.a: They learn which point in the night sky does not move.
items.why_vi: Chim non học phần trời đứng yên trong khi các sao khác quay quanh. A sai (không sinh ra đã biết); C sai (chúng coi ngôi sao khác là hướng bắc).
items.ev: Instead, young birds learn which part of the night sky stays still while the rest of the stars rotate around it.

items.q: What does the writer say about modern tracking devices?
o: They are too heavy for small birds.
They have shown that birds stop less often than expected.
They have replaced the need for experiments.
They are being used to reduce light pollution.
items.a: They have shown that birds stop less often than expected.
items.why_vi: "birds make far fewer stops than expected" (dừng ít hơn dự đoán nhiều). Thiết bị nặng dưới 1 gam nên A sai.
items.ev: Tracking devices weighing less than a gram can record the position of a bird, and some have revealed that birds make far fewer stops than expected.

de.title: The long story of glass
de.topic: The invention and uses of glass
de.gist: A history of glass from volcanic obsidian and early beads to glassblowing, Venetian glass, lenses, float glass and fibre optics.
de.vi: Đọc bài, làm 13 câu: nối tiêu đề, TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN, trả lời ngắn.
de.text:
The long story of glass

A. Glass is so common today that it is easy to forget how remarkable it is. It is made mainly from sand, which is heated until it melts and then cooled so quickly that its atoms do not have time to form crystals. Pure sand melts only at very high temperatures, so glassmakers add soda to lower the melting point and lime to make the finished glass strong and resistant to water. These basic ingredients have changed surprisingly little over thousands of years.

B. Long before people learned to make it, they used natural glass. When certain volcanoes erupt, lava can cool so fast that it forms obsidian, a black, glassy rock. Because obsidian breaks into pieces with extremely sharp edges, early humans used it for knives and arrowheads, and traded it over long distances. The oldest man-made glass objects that have been found are small beads from Mesopotamia, made more than 4,000 years ago. The Roman writer Pliny later told a story of sailors who cooked their food on a beach and discovered glass in the ashes of their fire, but historians believe the tale is probably not true, since an ordinary cooking fire is not hot enough to melt sand.

C. For many centuries glass remained a luxury. Objects were made by shaping hot glass around a core or by pressing it into moulds, which was slow and expensive. Everything changed in the first century BC, when craftsmen on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean discovered that they could blow air into a lump of hot glass through a metal tube. Glassblowing allowed a skilled worker to produce a cup or bottle in minutes. The Romans spread the technique across their empire, and glass drinking vessels became common even in ordinary homes. Fragments of Roman glass are still found at archaeological sites from Britain to North Africa.

D. In the Middle Ages, the most famous glass in Europe came from Venice. In 1291 the city ordered all of its glassmakers to move to the nearby island of Murano. Officially this was to protect Venice from fires, as the furnaces burned day and night, but it also made it easier to keep the methods of the craft secret. Glassmakers enjoyed a high social status, yet they were not allowed to leave the republic, and those who did risked severe punishment. In the fifteenth century, the workshops of Murano developed an exceptionally clear glass that was admired across the continent.

E. Glass also changed the way people see the world. Spectacles first appeared in northern Italy towards the end of the thirteenth century, allowing scholars and craftsmen to continue working as their eyesight weakened with age. Some three hundred years later, lens makers discovered that combining two lenses could make distant objects appear closer. The telescopes and microscopes of the seventeenth century revealed the moons of Jupiter and the cells of living things, and transformed science.

F. Flat glass for windows, however, was difficult to produce. For centuries it was made by spinning or rolling hot glass, and the result was often uneven and full of bubbles, so large windows were rare and expensive. The breakthrough came in the 1950s, when the British engineer Alastair Pilkington developed the float process. In this method, molten glass is poured onto a bath of molten tin, where it spreads out and forms a perfectly flat and even surface. Within a few decades, float glass had become the standard method for producing window glass around the world.

G. Today, some of the most important glass is almost invisible. Thin fibres of extremely pure glass are used in the cables that carry internet data as pulses of light under oceans and between cities. A single fibre, thinner than a human hair, can carry far more information than a copper wire. Meanwhile, chemists continue to develop new kinds of glass for phone screens, solar panels and medical devices, suggesting that one of the oldest materials made by humans still has a long future ahead of it. Glass can also be recycled again and again without losing quality, which is why many countries now collect used bottles and jars separately from other waste.

de.title: Pen or keyboard?
de.gist: An opinion article arguing that the choice between handwriting and typing in education should depend on the purpose of the task.
de.vi: Đọc bài, làm 13 câu: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN, nối nửa câu, trắc nghiệm.
de.text:
Pen or keyboard?

Few topics in education produce such strong feelings as the question of whether students should write by hand or type. On one side are those who see handwriting as a basic skill that is being lost; on the other are those who regard it as an old-fashioned habit that wastes valuable school time. In my view, both positions miss the point. The real question is not which tool is better in general, but which tool is better for a particular purpose.

Let us begin with what research can tell us. In one widely reported study, university students who took lecture notes by hand performed better on questions that required them to understand ideas than students who used laptops. The explanation offered was that typing is so fast that students tend to copy the lecturer word for word, while writing by hand forces them to select and summarise. This is an attractive idea, and it may well be true in some situations. However, later attempts to repeat the study produced mixed results, and I think it would be a mistake to treat a single experiment as final proof. Taking notes is, after all, only one part of learning, and much depends on what students do with their notes afterwards.

There is stronger evidence when it comes to young children. Learning to form letters by hand seems to help children recognise those letters when they read. Some brain imaging studies have found that areas linked to reading become more active after children practise writing letters than after they practise typing them. For this reason, I would argue that handwriting should remain a central part of the early primary curriculum, even if it takes up time that some would prefer to spend on other subjects.

At the same time, it is unrealistic to pretend that the keyboard is going away. Most adults now do the majority of their writing on screens, and many examinations at universities are already taken on computers. Students who type slowly are at a real disadvantage in these situations, not because they know less, but because they cannot get their ideas down quickly enough. Typing also makes it easier to correct mistakes and reorganise ideas, which matters a great deal in longer pieces of writing. It seems to me only fair that schools should teach typing as a skill in its own right, rather than expecting children to pick it up on their own.

The arguments are sometimes complicated by questions of cost. Laptops and tablets are expensive, and in schools with limited budgets, providing a device for every child can mean less money for books or teachers. Supporters of technology often reply that devices give students access to a world of information. That is true, but access to information is not the same as learning, and a classroom full of screens can also be a classroom full of distractions.

What, then, should schools do? I believe the most sensible approach is to match the tool to the task. When students are planning an essay, sketching a diagram or working through a mathematical problem, paper often allows a freedom that a screen does not. When they are producing a final draft, editing a long piece of work or collaborating with classmates, a keyboard is usually more efficient. Teachers are well placed to make these decisions, and they should be trusted to do so.

None of this is to say that handwriting has value only in the classroom. Many people still prefer to keep a paper diary, write a card by hand or jot down a shopping list on the back of an envelope. There is also a particular pleasure in receiving a handwritten letter that an email rarely matches. Whether these habits survive is a question for society as a whole. For schools, however, the goal should be students who can do both, and who know when each is appropriate.

de.title: Wetlands as flood defences
de.gist: A passage on how wetlands, coastal marshes and beaver dams reduce flooding, what has been lost and the limits of natural defences.
de.vi: Đọc bài, làm 13 câu: tìm đoạn chứa ý, nối đặc điểm, tóm tắt có khung từ.
de.text:
Wetlands as flood defences

A. Floods are among the most expensive natural hazards in the world, and many experts expect them to become more frequent as the climate changes. For most of the last century, the standard response was to build: rivers were lined with concrete walls, deepened and fitted with channels designed to move water away as quickly as possible. In recent years, however, engineers and planners have become increasingly interested in so-called nature-based solutions, and wetlands are at the centre of this discussion.

B. A wetland works rather like a sponge. When heavy rain falls, its soils and dense plants hold large amounts of water and then release it gradually over days or weeks. This slows the rate at which water reaches the river downstream and lowers the highest point of the flood. Some of the water also soaks slowly into the ground, where it refills the underground stores that supply wells and springs during dry periods. The hydrologist Dr Lena Fischer, who has modelled several river systems in central Europe, believes the effect can be considerable. "In our models, restoring a single large marsh upstream reduced the peak of a typical winter flood by around a fifth," she says. "For the town below, that can be the difference between wet streets and flooded homes."

C. Unfortunately, many wetlands have already been lost. Over centuries, they were drained to create farmland and to make room for towns and roads, and some estimates suggest that more than a third of the wetlands in the world have disappeared since 1970 alone. At the same time, many rivers were straightened. A straight channel carries water away from one place quickly, but in doing so it simply sends the flood downstream faster, often to communities that are less able to cope with it. In some regions, drainage ditches dug centuries ago are still maintained today, even where the land they protect is no longer farmed intensively.

D. Along coasts, salt marshes and mangrove forests play a similar role. Their roots hold sediment in place, and their branches and stems reduce the energy of waves before they reach the shore. During major storms, coastal villages protected by healthy marshes have often suffered less damage than similar villages nearby that had lost them. Professor Arun Mehta, who studies coastal protection, points out that such habitats also have a financial advantage. "A sea wall needs constant and costly repairs," he explains, "whereas a healthy mangrove belt maintains itself and can even grow as sea levels rise." He warns, though, that newly planted mangroves may take ten years or more to provide real protection, and that they need space that is often already used for housing or tourism.

E. In parts of Europe, an unexpected helper has returned. Beavers, which were hunted almost to extinction in many countries, have been reintroduced in a number of river catchments. The dams they build create chains of small ponds and wet areas that hold back water during storms. Beaver ponds also trap soil and pollutants carried by the water, so the river below them often runs clearer than before. Dr Sofia Ruiz, an ecologist who has worked with farming communities, says that the first reaction of many landowners was concern about flooded fields. "What changed attitudes was money," she says. "Once farmers were paid for the land that became wetter, most of them accepted the beavers quite happily."

F. Wetlands are not, however, a complete answer. Natural systems can reduce smaller and medium-sized floods, but the largest events may simply overwhelm them, and in densely populated areas there is rarely enough land to restore. For this reason, most specialists now argue for a combination of engineering and natural approaches rather than a choice between them. The case for wetlands is strengthened by the other benefits they provide. They are rich habitats for wildlife, they store large quantities of carbon in their soils, and they offer places for people to walk and relax. Few concrete walls can claim as much.

de.title: Farming upwards
de.gist: A passage explaining how vertical farms grow crops indoors in stacked layers, their advantages, costs and the crops they suit.
de.vi: Đọc bài, làm 13 câu: điền lưu đồ / ghi chú, TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN, trắc nghiệm.
de.text:
Farming upwards

By the middle of this century, around two thirds of the world's population is expected to live in cities. Feeding them will be a major challenge, particularly as farmland is lost to building and as droughts and floods become more common. One proposed solution is to bring farming into the city itself, and to grow crops not across fields but in tall stacks inside buildings. This approach, known as vertical farming, has attracted large amounts of investment over the last fifteen years.

A typical vertical farm is a closed warehouse or converted factory in which plants grow on shelves arranged one above another, sometimes reaching ten or more layers. Instead of soil, most farms use hydroponics, a method in which the roots of the plants hang in water containing the nutrients they need. Seeds are first planted in small blocks of material such as foam or coconut fibre. Once the seedlings have developed a few leaves, they are moved to the growing trays, where the water flows continuously past their roots. Light comes not from the sun but from LED lamps, which can be tuned to the exact colours that plants use most efficiently. Temperature and humidity are controlled by computers, and sensors check the condition of the plants many times a day. When the crop is ready, it is cut, packed and sent to shops, often on the same day.

Supporters point to several advantages. Because the environment is controlled, crops can be grown all year round regardless of the weather outside, and the same space can produce many harvests a year. As the water is collected and reused, vertical farms can use up to ninety per cent less water than traditional fields. There is also little need for pesticides, since insects find it hard to enter a sealed building. Finally, because the farms are located close to the people who eat the food, it does not need to travel hundreds of kilometres in refrigerated lorries. Some supermarkets also value the fact that the produce arrives clean and needs little washing.

The main difficulty is energy. Replacing sunlight with electric lighting is expensive, and heating, cooling and pumping water add further costs. Building a farm is expensive too, as the lighting, pumps and climate systems must all be installed before a single plant is grown. When electricity prices rose sharply in several countries in 2022, a number of well-known vertical farming companies closed or reduced their operations. Critics also point out that the environmental benefits depend heavily on where the electricity comes from. A farm powered by coal may produce more greenhouse gases per kilogram of lettuce than a field in the countryside, while one using wind or solar power can perform much better.

Cost also explains why vertical farms grow such a narrow range of crops. At present, they focus mainly on leafy greens such as lettuce and spinach, together with herbs like basil. These plants grow quickly, are small and light, and sell for a relatively high price. Staple crops such as wheat and rice, by contrast, are grown in enormous quantities, need a great deal of space and sell cheaply, so producing them indoors under lamps would make little economic sense.

Researchers are trying to change this picture. Some are breeding plant varieties that grow well under artificial light, while others are experimenting with robots that can plant, move and harvest trays with little human help. Others are testing ways of growing strawberries and tomatoes, which need more light and space than lettuce but can also sell for high prices. A few companies are building farms next to power stations or factories so that they can use waste heat. Whether these efforts will allow vertical farming to compete with traditional agriculture on a large scale is still uncertain. What seems likely is that it will play a useful role in supplying fresh vegetables to cities, rather than replacing fields altogether.

lines: Good morning, Westbrook Community Centre, Jenny speaking. How can I help?
Hello. I'd like to ask about hiring a hall for a party next month.
Of course. Can I take your name first?
Yes, it's Daniel Garrison. That's G-A-R-R-I-S-O-N. Garrison.
Thank you, Mr Garrison. And what kind of event is it?
It's a fortieth birthday party for my wife. It's a surprise, actually, so she doesn't know anything about it yet.
How lovely. And how many guests are you expecting?
About 70, I think. Maybe a few more if her cousins come from Scotland.

Then I'd recommend the Garden Room rather than the Main Hall. The Main Hall holds two hundred people, so with seventy guests it would feel rather empty. The Garden Room takes up to eighty, and it opens onto the terrace, which is nice on a summer evening.
That sounds perfect. How much does it cost?
For an evening booking, that's from six o'clock until midnight, it's 320 pounds.
And does that include tables and chairs?
Yes, it does, and our staff set them up for you before you arrive. The only extra charge is for cleaning, which is forty-five pounds.

I see. What about music? We were hoping to have a small band.
Live music is allowed, but it has to finish by 11:30 because there are houses right next to the centre. After that you can play quiet background music until midnight.

There's a car park behind the centre with thirty spaces. It's normally two pounds an hour, but parking is free after six o'clock, so your guests won't have to pay.
Great. So how do I book?
I need a deposit of one hundred pounds to hold the date. You can pay by bank transfer, or by card over the phone.

lines: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hollybank Community Garden. My name's Rachel, and I coordinate the volunteers here. Before we start work, I'd like to tell you a little about how the garden runs.

The garden opened eight years ago on land that used to be a car park. Most people assume the local council paid for it, but in fact the money came from a group of local businesses, and the council simply agreed to lease us the land.

We now have around a hundred and twenty volunteers, although on a typical Saturday only about twenty turn up. That's why we ask everyone to sign up for at least one shift a month on the website, so we know how many people to expect.

Now, safety. You'll find gloves in the green shed, and please wear them whenever you're handling soil. The one rule we're really strict about is that children under twelve must stay with an adult at all times, because some of our tools are very sharp.
Let me take you round the different areas. If you look at the map in your welcome pack, the entrance is at the bottom.

Just inside the gate, on your left, is the herb spiral. It looks like a small stone tower. This is where our youngest volunteers work, because the herbs are easy to look after, and today a school group will be planting mint and basil there.
Behind the herb spiral you'll see the greenhouse. We grow tomatoes and peppers in there, but at this time of year the main job is watering, and on hot days that needs doing twice.
In the far corner is the orchard. The apple trees are quite old now, and our main task there this month is pruning them, which means cutting back the dead branches. Don't worry, we'll show you how.

Next to the orchard is the pond. It's become home to frogs and dragonflies, and once a week we record which species we see for a university project. You don't need any experience, just a good pair of eyes.
Finally, near the café is the compost area. Kitchen waste from the café goes in there, and volunteers turn the heaps with forks every Wednesday. It's hard work, but it's great exercise.
The café itself is run by volunteers too, and all the profits go back into the garden, mostly to buy seeds and repair the tools.

Right, the last thing before we split into groups: our open day is on the twenty-first of September, and we need people to help with the plant sale and guided tours. If you're interested, please put your name on the list by the café door.

de.gist: Two students discuss their research project on classroom noise with their tutor.
de.vi: Nghe thảo luận, chọn đáp án rồi nối ý kiến với người nói.
lines: So, Owen and Lily, how is your project on classroom noise going?
Quite well, I think. We've measured the noise in six primary school classrooms, using a sound meter on the teacher's desk.
And how long did you spend in each classroom? A single lesson can be very different from a whole day.

We stayed for a full school day in each one, from nine until three, and the meter took a reading every minute. That gave us more than three hundred readings per room, so we could compare lessons, group work and lunch breaks.
Although we did have one problem. In the first school, the children kept touching the meter, so the readings were much higher than normal. In the end we had to repeat all those measurements.
That's a common issue. And what did you find?

The average level during lessons was around sixty-five decibels. What surprised us most was that the noisiest classrooms weren't the ones with the most children. They were the ones with hard floors and high ceilings.
So the room itself mattered more than the class size.
Exactly. One classroom had a carpet and soft boards on the walls, and even with thirty children it was the quietest of the six.
Good. Now, you also interviewed teachers, didn't you?
Yes, eight of them. Most said the noise made them tired by the end of the day, but they were more worried about the children who sit at the back, because those children often miss instructions.
A couple of teachers also mentioned that they have to raise their voices, and one had actually lost her voice twice this year.
Did any of the teachers have ideas about why the noise builds up during the day?

Several of them said that once the background noise rises, children start speaking more loudly so that their friends can hear them, and then everyone else does the same. One teacher called it a kind of chain reaction.
That's very relevant. Have you decided how to present your findings?
We were going to write a standard report, but we think a short video would show the difference between the rooms more clearly, so people can actually hear it.
That's a good idea, but remember the department still requires a written summary of about a thousand words to go with it.
Now, before you finish, I'd like you to think about recommendations. Owen, what would you suggest?
Personally, I'd put carpets in every classroom. It's the cheapest change and it made the biggest difference in our data.
I'm not so sure. Carpets are hard to keep clean, and some children have allergies. I'd rather see schools use soft wall panels, which can be cleaned easily.
My own view is that you should also mention teacher training. Simple routines, like a signal for silence, can reduce noise without any building work at all.
That's true. And I think the schools should measure noise regularly themselves. Cheap meters are easy to buy now.
And I'd add that new schools should be designed with sound in mind from the start, because changing a building later is far more expensive.

de.vi: Nghe bài giảng, điền ghi chú (MỖI CHỖ MỘT TỪ).
lines: Good afternoon. Today I'm going to talk about how elephants communicate, a subject that has changed a great deal in the last forty years.

For a long time, scientists believed that elephants were fairly quiet animals. Apart from the famous trumpeting, which is mostly used when they are excited or alarmed, they seemed to make very few sounds.

That view changed in the 1980s, when a researcher working at a zoo noticed a kind of throbbing in the air near the elephants, rather like the feeling you get near a large organ in a church. She suspected the animals were producing sounds that were too low for humans to hear.

Recordings proved her right. Elephants make deep rumbles, many of them below the range of human hearing. Sound at these very low frequencies is called infrasound, and its great advantage is that it travels long distances without fading, even through forest.

To give you an idea of how low these sounds are, the lowest note that most people can hear is about twenty hertz, while some elephant rumbles go down to around fourteen. We may not hear them, but we can sometimes feel them.

In good conditions, especially in the cool air of the evening, a rumble can be heard by other elephants several kilometres away. So when a group appears to be moving in the same direction without any visible signal, they may in fact be talking to each other.

Researchers have since identified different kinds of rumble. There is a greeting rumble when family members meet after a separation, and a quite different rumble that females use when they are ready to mate. Mothers also use a soft rumble to keep in contact with their calves.
Adult males in a condition known as musth, when their hormone levels are very high, produce a particular low rumble that seems to warn other males to keep their distance.
The second discovery was even more surprising. Some of the energy from a rumble travels through the ground as vibration, and elephants appear to detect these vibrations through their feet.

The soles of their feet contain special nerve endings that are sensitive to vibration. When elephants are listening in this way, they often lean forward and press their feet into the ground, and sometimes they lift one foot off the ground altogether.

Field experiments support this. When researchers played recorded warning calls through the ground, rather than through the air, the elephants still reacted. They gathered their young together and moved away from the source.

Of course, elephants do not rely on sound alone. Their sense of smell is extremely good, and the trunk plays a central role. An elephant can identify other members of its family from their scent, and males can tell from smell whether a female is ready to mate.
Touch is also important. Elephants greet each other by placing the tip of the trunk in the other animal's mouth, and calves are constantly touched and guided by the adults around them.

Why does all this matter? Understanding elephant communication can help with conservation. For example, in some areas farmers are now using recorded calls to keep elephants away from their crops without harming them.
In the final part of the lecture, I'll look at how noise from roads and mining may be interfering with these low-frequency signals.

groups.inst: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.q: Old view: elephants seemed quiet; trumpeting used mainly when excited or ______
items.why_vi: "trumpeting, which is mostly used when they are excited or alarmed".
items.ev: Apart from the famous trumpeting, which is mostly used when they are excited or alarmed, they seemed to make very few sounds.

items.q: 1980s: researcher at a ______ felt a throbbing in the air
items.why_vi: "a researcher working at a zoo noticed a kind of throbbing in the air".
items.ev: That view changed in the 1980s, when a researcher working at a zoo noticed a kind of throbbing in the air near the elephants, rather like the feeling you get near a large organ in a church.

items.q: Very low sound (infrasound) travels far without ______
items.why_vi: "travels long distances without fading" (không yếu đi).
items.ev: Sound at these very low frequencies is called infrasound, and its great advantage is that it travels long distances without fading, even through forest.

items.q: Rumbles carry best in the cool air of the ______
items.why_vi: "especially in the cool air of the evening".
items.ev: In good conditions, especially in the cool air of the evening, a rumble can be heard by other elephants several kilometres away.

items.q: Mothers use a soft rumble to stay in contact with their ______
items.why_vi: "Mothers also use a soft rumble to keep in contact with their calves" (voi con).
items.ev: Mothers also use a soft rumble to keep in contact with their calves.

items.q: Vibrations through the ground are detected through the ______
items.why_vi: "elephants appear to detect these vibrations through their feet".
items.ev: Some of the energy from a rumble travels through the ground as vibration, and elephants appear to detect these vibrations through their feet.

items.q: When listening this way, they may lift one foot off the ______
items.why_vi: "sometimes they lift one foot off the ground altogether".
items.ev: When elephants are listening in this way, they often lean forward and press their feet into the ground, and sometimes they lift one foot off the ground altogether.

items.q: Experiment: after warning calls played through the ground, elephants gathered their ______
items.why_vi: "They gathered their young together and moved away" (gom con nhỏ lại).
items.ev: They gathered their young together and moved away from the source.

items.q: Smell: family members are recognised by their ______
items.why_vi: "identify other members of its family from their scent" (mùi).
items.ev: An elephant can identify other members of its family from their scent, and males can tell from smell whether a female is ready to mate.

items.q: Conservation: recorded calls keep elephants away from farmers' ______
items.why_vi: "using recorded calls to keep elephants away from their crops" (mùa màng).
items.ev: For example, in some areas farmers are now using recorded calls to keep elephants away from their crops without harming them.

de.title: Part 5 · Bộ 1: văn phòng và khách hàng
de.gist: Ten business sentences testing word forms, verbs, prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns, comparison and vocabulary.
de.vi: Chọn từ đúng điền vào chỗ trống.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The new booking system has made it much ------- for customers to change their reservations online.
items.why_vi: Sau "much" và trước "for" cần tính từ so sánh hơn: "much easier" (dễ hơn nhiều). "easily" là trạng từ, "ease" là danh từ.

items.q: Ms. Patel was praised for her ------- handling of the difficult client meeting.
items.why_vi: Trước danh từ "handling" cần tính từ bổ nghĩa: "professional handling". "professionally" là trạng từ, không đứng trước danh từ.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: By the time the auditors arrive next Monday, the finance team ------- all of the quarterly reports.
items.why_vi: "By the time + hiện tại đơn" nói về mốc tương lai, việc xong trước mốc đó dùng tương lai hoàn thành: "will have completed".

items.q: All visitors are required ------- a badge at the reception desk before entering the factory.
items.why_vi: Cấu trúc "be required to + động từ nguyên mẫu": bắt buộc phải làm gì.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The marketing report must be submitted ------- Friday afternoon at the latest.
items.why_vi: "by + thời điểm" = trước hoặc đúng hạn đó (hạn chót). "until" là kéo dài liên tục tới lúc đó, không hợp với "submitted".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: ------- the printer was repaired last week, it still jams when printing on both sides.
items.why_vi: Hai vế trái ngược (đã sửa nhưng vẫn kẹt giấy) nên dùng "Although" + mệnh đề. "Despite" phải đi với danh từ, không đi với mệnh đề.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Employees ------- have not yet registered for the safety training should contact Human Resources.
items.why_vi: Đại từ quan hệ chỉ người làm chủ ngữ của "have not yet registered" là "who". "whom" là tân ngữ, "which" chỉ vật.

items.q: Mr. Chen prefers to check the shipping documents -------, rather than asking his assistant to do it.
items.why_vi: Đại từ phản thân "himself" nhấn mạnh tự mình làm, đối lập với việc nhờ trợ lý.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: This year's trade fair attracted ------- exhibitors than any previous event in the city.
items.why_vi: Có "than" nên cần so sánh hơn: "more exhibitors than". "exhibitors" đếm được nên không dùng "much".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Please keep your receipt, as it is needed to ------- a refund within thirty days of purchase.
items.why_vi: Cụm cố định "claim a refund" = yêu cầu hoàn tiền. Các từ khác không đi với "refund" theo nghĩa này.

de.title: Part 5 · Bộ 2: sản xuất và giao hàng
de.gist: Ten business sentences about factories, deliveries and suppliers testing grammar and vocabulary.
de.vi: Chọn từ đúng điền vào chỗ trống.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The factory has increased its output ------- since the new assembly line was installed in March.
items.why_vi: Bổ nghĩa cho động từ "has increased" cần trạng từ: "increased its output significantly".

items.q: Customers who place an order before noon will receive ------- of their goods on the same day.
items.why_vi: Sau động từ "receive" và trước "of" cần danh từ: "receive delivery of" (nhận hàng).

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The damaged boxes ------- to the supplier yesterday, and replacements are expected on Thursday.
items.why_vi: Hộp hàng không tự trả về nên dùng bị động; có "yesterday" nên dùng quá khứ đơn bị động "were returned".

items.q: If the shipment had left the port on time, it ------- at the warehouse by now.
items.why_vi: Câu điều kiện loại 3 (giả định trái với quá khứ): "If + had + V3, would have + V3".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: All orders over $200 are shipped free of charge, regardless ------- the destination.
items.why_vi: Cụm cố định "regardless of" = bất kể.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The supplier offered a large discount; -------, the purchasing manager decided to sign a two-year contract.
items.why_vi: Vế sau là kết quả của vế trước (được giảm giá nên ký hợp đồng): dùng "therefore" (vì vậy).

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The two companies agreed to share ------- research facilities in order to reduce costs.
items.why_vi: Trước cụm danh từ "research facilities" cần tính từ sở hữu "their".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Not only ------- the new packaging cheaper, but it is also easier to recycle.
items.why_vi: "Not only" đứng đầu câu thì đảo trợ động từ lên trước chủ ngữ: "Not only is the new packaging cheaper".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Due to high demand, the blue model is temporarily out of -------, but more units will arrive next week.
items.why_vi: Cụm cố định "out of stock" = hết hàng. "out of order" là hỏng (máy móc).

items.q: The contract will ------- automatically at the end of the year unless either party cancels it in writing.
items.why_vi: Hợp đồng "renew" = gia hạn. Các từ khác không dùng cho hợp đồng.

de.title: Part 5 · Bộ 3: tuyển dụng và đào tạo
de.topic: Hiring, staff training and workplace events
de.gist: Ten business sentences about recruitment, training and company events testing grammar and vocabulary.
de.vi: Chọn từ đúng điền vào chỗ trống.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Applicants must provide two ------- from previous employers along with their application form.
items.why_vi: Sau số "two" cần danh từ số nhiều: "two references" (hai thư giới thiệu).

items.q: The training session was so ------- that several staff members asked for a second one.
items.why_vi: Sau "was so" cần tính từ: "so informative" (rất bổ ích).

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Mr. Lopez ------- for the company for fifteen years when he was promoted to regional director.
items.why_vi: Việc kéo dài 15 năm xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ ("was promoted") nên dùng quá khứ hoàn thành "had worked".

items.q: We look forward to ------- you at the annual awards dinner on December 12.
items.why_vi: "look forward to" có "to" là giới từ nên theo sau là V-ing: "look forward to seeing".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Interviews for the sales position will take place ------- 9:00 A.M. and 4:00 P.M. on Wednesday.
items.why_vi: Cấu trúc "between A and B" = trong khoảng từ A đến B.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: New employees cannot access the main database ------- they have completed the security course.
items.why_vi: "cannot … until" = không thể … cho đến khi: chỉ được vào cơ sở dữ liệu sau khi học xong khoá an ninh.

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The manager thanked the volunteers, ------- of whom had given up their weekend to help at the event.
items.why_vi: Cấu trúc "many of whom" thay cho người đếm được (volunteers). "much" dùng cho không đếm được; "every" không đứng trước "of whom".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: The more experience candidates have, the ------- their chances of being offered the job.
items.why_vi: Cấu trúc so sánh kép "The more …, the + so sánh hơn": "the better their chances".

groups.inst: Choose the best answer to complete the sentence.

items.q: Staff who wish to ------- the leadership workshop should sign up on the intranet by Friday.
items.why_vi: "attend a workshop" = tham dự hội thảo, đi thẳng với tân ngữ. "participate" cần "in"; "assist" là giúp đỡ.

items.q: The company offers a generous ------- package, including health insurance and paid holidays.
items.why_vi: Cụm "benefits package" = gói phúc lợi (bảo hiểm, nghỉ phép có lương).

de.title: Part 6 · Thư báo bảo trì thang máy
de.gist: An email from building management tells tenants that the elevators will be closed for maintenance on a Saturday.
de.vi: Đọc thư, chọn đáp án cho 4 chỗ trống.
de.text:
To: All tenants, Harbor Point Office Tower
From: Building Management
Subject: Elevator maintenance

Please note that the two main elevators will be closed for maintenance on Saturday, May 18, from 7:00 A.M. to 3:00 P.M. During this time, the service elevator at the rear of the building will [1] available for staff who need to come in.

[2] We have scheduled the work for a weekend in order to cause as little disruption as possible.

The maintenance team will replace the control panels and test the emergency brakes, so the work cannot be [3]. If you have deliveries arriving that day, please ask the courier to use the loading entrance on Mill Street.

We apologize for any [4] and thank you for your patience.

groups.inst: Read the text. Choose the best answer for each gap.

items.q: Gap 1
items.why_vi: Sau "will" cần động từ nguyên mẫu: "will remain available" (vẫn dùng được).

items.q: Gap 2
o: We expect fewer people than usual to be in the building on that day.
The new elevators were installed only two years ago.
Tenants are reminded that smoking is not allowed in the lobby.
Our office will be closed on Monday for the public holiday.
items.a: We expect fewer people than usual to be in the building on that day.
items.why_vi: Câu sau nói chọn ngày cuối tuần để ít ảnh hưởng nhất; câu chèn hợp mạch là "ngày đó ít người trong toà nhà hơn thường lệ". Các câu khác lạc ý hoặc mâu thuẫn (thay bảng điều khiển chứ không nói thang mới lắp).

items.q: Gap 3
items.why_vi: Việc thay bảng điều khiển và thử phanh khẩn cấp cần cẩn thận nên "cannot be hurried" (không thể làm vội). "postponed" (hoãn) không hợp vì lịch đã định.

items.q: Gap 4
items.why_vi: Sau "any" trong cụm "apologize for any …" cần danh từ: "any inconvenience" (mọi bất tiện).

de.title: Part 6 · Quảng cáo lớp học buổi tối
de.gist: An advertisement for an evening business writing course at a community college.
de.vi: Đọc quảng cáo, chọn đáp án cho 4 chỗ trống.
de.text:
Write with Confidence: Business Writing for Professionals

Do your emails take too long to write? Are your reports [1] than they need to be? Our eight-week evening course at Lakeside Community College will help you communicate clearly and quickly at work.

Classes meet every Tuesday from 6:30 to 8:30 P.M. [2] Each session focuses on a different type of document, such as proposals, meeting minutes and customer replies.

Participants will receive personal feedback on their writing [3] the course. The instructor, Ms. Grace Okafor, has trained staff at more than forty companies.

The fee is $280, which includes all materials. Many employers will cover the cost, so be sure to ask your manager. [4] early, as places are limited to fifteen people per class.

groups.inst: Read the text. Choose the best answer for each gap.

items.q: Gap 1
items.why_vi: Có "than" phía sau nên cần so sánh hơn: "longer than they need to be".

items.q: Gap 2
o: The first class begins on September 9.
The college library is open until 10:00 P.M.
Last year's course was taught online.
Parking near the college is very expensive.
items.a: The first class begins on September 9.
items.why_vi: Câu trước nói lịch học hằng tuần, câu chèn nêu ngày bắt đầu khoá là hợp mạch. Câu "năm ngoái học trực tuyến" lạc ý; câu thư viện và bãi đỗ xe không liên quan.

items.q: Gap 3
items.why_vi: "throughout the course" = suốt cả khoá học. Các giới từ khác không đi với khoảng thời gian như vậy.

items.q: Gap 4
items.why_vi: Câu mệnh lệnh mở đầu bằng động từ nguyên mẫu: "Register early" (đăng ký sớm).

de.title: Part 6 · Thông báo đổi nhà cung cấp cà phê
de.topic: Office memo about a new coffee supplier
de.gist: A memo tells staff that the office is changing its coffee supplier and explains the new ordering process.
de.vi: Đọc thông báo nội bộ, chọn đáp án cho 4 chỗ trống.
de.text:
MEMO
To: All staff
From: Daniel Reyes, Office Manager
Re: New coffee supplier

Starting next month, the office will buy its coffee and tea from Greenbean Supplies [1] our current supplier. After comparing several companies, we found that Greenbean offers better prices and delivers twice a week.

The new machines will be installed in both kitchens on Friday afternoon. [2] Please do not use the kitchens between 2:00 and 4:00 P.M. on that day.

If your team needs extra supplies for meetings, you can now order them [3] through the office supply page on the intranet. Orders placed before noon will arrive the next working day.

Please send any comments about the change to me [4] the end of the month.

groups.inst: Read the text. Choose the best answer for each gap.

items.q: Gap 1
items.why_vi: Đổi nhà cung cấp: mua của Greenbean "instead of" (thay cho) nhà cung cấp hiện tại. "in addition to" (thêm vào) trái với ý đổi.

items.q: Gap 2
o: The technicians will need about two hours to complete the work.
Greenbean was founded in 1995 by two brothers.
Our old machines are less than a year old.
Tea is more popular than coffee in our office.
items.a: The technicians will need about two hours to complete the work.
items.why_vi: Câu sau yêu cầu không dùng bếp từ 2 đến 4 giờ; câu chèn "thợ cần khoảng hai giờ" giải thích vì sao. Câu "máy cũ chưa tới một năm" mâu thuẫn với việc thay máy; các câu khác lạc ý.

items.q: Gap 3
items.why_vi: Bổ nghĩa cho động từ "order" cần trạng từ: "order them directly" (đặt trực tiếp).

items.q: Gap 4
items.why_vi: "by the end of the month" = trước cuối tháng (hạn chót).

de.title: Part 7 · Email đổi lịch giao hàng
de.topic: Email about a delayed furniture delivery
de.gist: A furniture company emails a customer to explain a delivery delay and offer two options.
de.vi: Đọc email, chọn đáp án đúng.
de.text:
### Email
To: Priya Sharma <p.sharma@brightlaw.com>
From: Customer Service, Oakline Office Furniture
Date: April 3
Subject: Your order #44817

Dear Ms. Sharma,

Thank you for ordering twelve Alder desks and twelve Ridge chairs for your new office. [1] Unfortunately, our factory in Portland has had a problem with one of its cutting machines, and the desks will not be ready by April 10 as planned. [2]

The chairs are already in our warehouse. We can deliver them on April 10 as scheduled and bring the desks on April 24, at no extra cost. Alternatively, we can deliver the complete order together on April 24. [3]

To apologize for the delay, we would like to offer you a 10 percent discount on the desks. This will be refunded to your credit card once the delivery is complete. [4]

Please reply to this email by April 6 to tell us which option you prefer. If we do not hear from you, we will deliver everything on April 24.

Kind regards,
Marcus Bell
Customer Service Team

groups.inst: Read the email. Choose the best answer to each question.

items.q: What is the main purpose of the email?
o: To explain a delay and offer delivery options
To confirm that an order has been delivered
To advertise a new range of office chairs
To ask Ms. Sharma to pay an overdue bill
items.a: To explain a delay and offer delivery options
items.why_vi: Email báo bàn chưa kịp làm (máy cắt hỏng) và đưa hai cách giao hàng. Đây là câu hỏi mục đích, đọc đoạn đầu và đoạn hai.
items.ev: Unfortunately, our factory in Portland has had a problem with one of its cutting machines, and the desks will not be ready by April 10 as planned.

items.q: What will happen if Ms. Sharma does not reply by April 6?
o: The chairs will be delivered on April 10.
Everything will be delivered on April 24.
She will lose the 10 percent discount.
items.a: Everything will be delivered on April 24.
items.why_vi: Câu cuối: không trả lời thì giao tất cả ngày 24/4. Bẫy: "April 10" là ngày giao ghế nếu chọn cách thứ nhất.
items.ev: If we do not hear from you, we will deliver everything on April 24.

items.q: What is indicated about the discount?
o: It applies to both desks and chairs.
It will be paid back after delivery.
It must be requested by April 6.
It is offered only to new customers.
items.a: It will be paid back after delivery.
items.why_vi: Khoản giảm 10% chỉ cho bàn và được hoàn vào thẻ sau khi giao xong ("refunded … once the delivery is complete").
items.ev: This will be refunded to your credit card once the delivery is complete.

items.q: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? "We are very sorry for this inconvenience."
items.why_vi: Câu xin lỗi hợp nhất ngay sau tin xấu "bàn không kịp giao ngày 10/4", tức vị trí [2]. Ở [1] chưa có gì để xin lỗi; [3], [4] đã sang chuyện lựa chọn và giảm giá.

de.title: Part 7 · Chuỗi tin nhắn về phòng họp
de.topic: Text-message chain about a meeting room
de.gist: Two colleagues message each other to solve a meeting-room problem before a client visit.
de.vi: Đọc chuỗi tin nhắn, chọn đáp án đúng.
de.text:
### Text-message chain
Helen Wong (9:12 A.M.): Hi Tom, are you in the office yet? The projector in Room 4B isn't working, and the Dalton clients arrive at 10:30.
Tom Baker (9:14 A.M.): I'm on the train, about twenty minutes away. Have you called the IT help desk?
Helen Wong (9:15 A.M.): Yes, but they said a technician can't come until the afternoon.
Tom Baker (9:17 A.M.): OK. Room 2A has a large screen, and I think it's free this morning. Could you check the booking system?
Helen Wong (9:21 A.M.): You're right, nobody has booked it until 1:00. I've reserved it from 10:00 to 12:00.
Tom Baker (9:22 A.M.): Great. Can you ask reception to send the clients to the second floor?
Helen Wong (9:23 A.M.): Leave it to me. I'll also move the coffee and pastries there.
Tom Baker (9:24 A.M.): Thanks, Helen. I'll bring the printed contracts when I arrive.

groups.inst: Read the text-message chain. Choose the best answer to each question.

items.q: Why did Ms. Wong contact Mr. Baker?
o: A piece of equipment is not working.
A client has canceled a meeting.
She cannot find the printed contracts.
The train to the office is late.
items.a: A piece of equipment is not working.
items.why_vi: Tin đầu: máy chiếu phòng 4B hỏng trong khi khách tới lúc 10:30.
items.ev: The projector in Room 4B isn't working, and the Dalton clients arrive at 10:30.

de.title: Part 7 · Thông báo chương trình xe đạp công ty
de.gist: A notice describes a new company program that helps staff buy bicycles and lists its rules.
de.vi: Đọc thông báo, chọn đáp án đúng.
de.text:
### Notice
Ride2Work: New Cycling Program for Staff

From June 1, Corvan Logistics will help employees buy a bicycle for travelling to work. Under the Ride2Work program, the company pays for the bicycle up front, and employees repay the cost through small monthly deductions from their salary over twelve months. There is no interest to pay.

Any permanent employee who has worked for the company for at least six months may apply. Bicycles must be bought from one of our three partner shops, which are listed on the staff website. The maximum value is $1,200, including a helmet and lights.

To help riders, secure bicycle parking has been added in the basement of the Riverside building, and showers are available on the ground floor. Lockers can be requested from the facilities team.

Application forms are available from Human Resources. Completed forms should be returned by May 20. Please note that the program cannot be used to buy electric scooters.

groups.inst: Read the notice. Choose the best answer to each question.

items.q: What is the purpose of the notice?
o: To introduce a program for buying bicycles
To announce the opening of a bicycle shop
To explain new rules for company cars
To invite staff to a cycling competition
items.a: To introduce a program for buying bicycles
items.why_vi: Thông báo giới thiệu chương trình Ride2Work: công ty trả trước tiền xe đạp, nhân viên trả dần.
items.ev: From June 1, Corvan Logistics will help employees buy a bicycle for travelling to work.

items.q: The word "secure" in paragraph 3, line 1, is closest in meaning to
items.why_vi: "secure bicycle parking" = chỗ để xe an toàn (không bị mất). "certain" là chắc chắn, "confident" là tự tin, không hợp với chỗ để xe.
items.ev: To help riders, secure bicycle parking has been added in the basement of the Riverside building, and showers are available on the ground floor.

items.q: What is NOT mentioned as part of the program?
o: Payments are spread over a year.
Bicycles must come from partner shops.
The company provides free bicycle repairs.
items.a: The company provides free bicycle repairs.
items.why_vi: Câu NOT: ba ý kia đều có trong bài (trả trong 12 tháng, không lãi, mua ở cửa hàng đối tác). Sửa xe miễn phí không được nhắc.

items.q: Who can apply for the program?
o: Permanent staff with at least six months of service
Any employee who already owns a bicycle
Only staff working in the Riverside building
Temporary workers who live near the office
items.a: Permanent staff with at least six months of service
items.why_vi: Đoạn hai: nhân viên chính thức đã làm ít nhất sáu tháng được đăng ký.
items.ev: Any permanent employee who has worked for the company for at least six months may apply.
